title: WPMS/17227/1988 of SRI KANHAI Vs D.J.DEHRADUN and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 732 of 2004 (M/S)
Sri Kanhai .....Petitioner
Versus
D.J. Dehradun and others .....Respondents
Mr. Rajat Mittal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State.
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Writ Petition was dismissed on 01.09.2004 for non
prosecution. Undisputedly, no notice was served upon
the petitioner after transfer of the present writ petition
from the Allahabad High Court to this High Court.
Therefore, dismissal of the writ petition on 01.09.2004
without notice seems to be totally unjustified.
Consequently, restoration application No. 221 of 2014 is
allowed. Order dated 01.09.2004 is hereby recalled.
Writ petition is restored to its original number.
CLMA No.4741 of 2014 & CLMA No. 4742 of 2014
Original petitioner is reported to have died on
01.02.1989 leaving behind applicants as LRs of the
original petitioner. For the reasons shown, delay in
moving substitution application is condoned. CLMA
No. 4741 of 2014 stands disposed of.
 For the reasons stated in the application,
substitution application No. 4742 of 2014 is allowed.
Let applicants be substituted as legal heirs of the
deceased petitioner.
CLMA No.5274 of 2014 & CLMA No. 5275 of 2014
 It is reported that respondent No.3 has expired
leaving behind legal heirs as mentioned in paragraph
No. 13 of the substitution application. Since original

2
petitioner also expired and writ petition was dismissed
for non-prosecution after transfer from the Allahabad
High Court, therefore, reasons for seeking condonation
of delay in moving the substitution application, seems to
be justified. Consequently, delay condonation
application is allowed. Delay in moving substitution
application is condoned.
 Since persons shown in paragraph No. 13 of the
application are legal heirs of respondent No.3, therefore,
they are permitted to be substituted as legal heirs of
respondent No.3. CLMA No. 5275 of 2014 stands
disposed of. Let necessary amendment in the memo of
parties may be carried out within 48 hrs.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
present petition may be heard finally today itself.
 Present petition is filed assailing the order dated
12.05.1988, passed by the District Judge, Dehradun
whereby Civil Revision No. 74 of 1987 filed by the
respondent No. 3, defendant/ respondent No.3 was
allowed and it was held that Civil Court had absolutely
no jurisdiction over the Suit in question and plaint
ought to have been returned for the presentation before
the competent Court.
 Undisputedly, name of the plaintiff is not recorded
in the revenue record. Case of the plaintiff is that he is
the owner of the property in question and the property
was illegally transferred without his knowledge.
Therefore, sale deed is void and is liable to be cancelled.
Since name of the petitioner is not mutated in the
revenue record, he has to file suit for declaration seeking
his title as well as for declaring the impugned sale deed

3
void. It goes without saying if plaintiff is able to prove
himself to be bhumidhar of the property, sale deed in
question shall be void.
 In view of the above, I do not find any illegality or
perversity in the impugned order. Writ petition is
devoid of merit and is hereby dismissed. However, it is
directed that learned Trial Court shall return the plaint
to the plaintiff within 30 days from today for the
presentation before the appropriate court. Plaintiff
may institute suit before the competent Revenue Court
after serving statutory notice and after carrying
necessary amendments therein. It is made clear, if suit
is presented before the Revenue Court within next 90
days, same shall not be dismissed on the ground of
limitation and shall be decided at its own merit in
accordance with law.
